search_row.title: Evolutionarily stable strategy conditions
search_row.statement: A strategy is evolutionarily stable if, once common, it cannot be invaded by any rare alternative strategy.
search_row.math: I is an ESS iff for all J \ne I: E(I,I) > E(J,I), or E(I,I) = E(J,I) and E(I,J) > E(J,J); every ESS is an asymptotically stable rest point of the replicator dynamics (Taylor and Jonker 1978), not conversely

fields.dct:source: John Maynard Smith (1973) The Logic of Animal Conflict
fields.delphi:proposedTest: In a system with measurable payoffs (microbial public-goods strains, contest behaviour), estimate the payoff matrix and test that the predicted ESS composition resists experimental invasion by rare alternative strategies.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: an infinite, well-mixed population with pairwise interactions and asexual or clonal inheritance of strategies. Formal status: the definition is exact, and the link to replicator dynamics is proved. Finite populations, mutation and genetic constraints can stop an ESS from being reached.
